licences.notes: Words as printed in the Peters vocal score (Secondate with no comma; desiri; and pene; with semicolons; Dea with a capital). The print has “mici” for miei in bar 31 (both men) and bar 35 (Ferrando); the word keeps the printed letters, with the IPA and meaning of miei.

licences.source: Edition Peters vocal score (Edition Peters Nr. 4474, plate 11446, edited by Georg Schünemann), pages 224–227, bars 1–71 of No. 21
licences.author: Kurt Soldan (1891–1946), piano reduction
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: sung lines and piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, a separate sweep for dynamics and other marks, then checked bar by bar by a fresh checker (one error found and corrected: a staccato in the right hand in bar 31 that is not printed). The German singing translation is left out. The chorus of musicians (sopranos, altos, tenors and basses, bars 59–69) has a staff for each part and is heard with the piano; it has no role here. Where the print gives the basses no words, they sing the tenors' words. Playback tempo: an eighth note = 76 (♩ = 38), from Jacobs (3:12 with the recitative before it); Mozart gives the word Andante only.
